en: We have this oration from the library of Maximus Margunius. It was translated into Latin long ago by Achilles Statius, a Portuguese, whose version was sent to me from Rome by Fr Hieronymus Brunellus, priest of our Society, after I had made this new one. The author of this oration is Sophronius, patriarch of Jerusalem, whose anniversary Greeks and Latins keep on 2 March. The Greeks give this eulogy: 'Of our holy father Sophronius, patriarch of Jerusalem, of Damascus by birth, distinguished by manifold learning, knowledge of the divine writings and piety. He flourished under Heraclius, in whose 19th year he was raised to that see and died in the 28th: When, as Cedrenus says, he had long and much contended against Heraclius and Sergius and Pyrrhus the Monothelites who agreed with him,' and had left many writings to the Church, among them the book entitled Pratum spirituale; the Life of Mary of Egypt, various encomia on saints, two homilies on the cross; and the synodical Epistle to Pope John and to Sergius, bishop of Constantinople. See Cedrenus and Zonaras on Heraclius. Sophronius delivered this oration on the eve of the Exaltation of the holy Cross, i.e. 13 September, the day on which the dedication of the temple at Jerusalem, called the Anastasis or Resurrection, is celebrated. The Typicon of Sabas, on the 13th day: 'The dedication of the holy Resurrection of Christ our God.' And in this whole oration Sophronius speaks of this resurrection, not of the feast of the Resurrection or Easter.
text: Habemus hanc orationem ex bibliotheca Maximi Margunii. Latine versa est jam olim ab Achille Statio, Lusitano, cujus versio, postquam hanc novam confeceram, Roma ad me missa est a R. P. Hieronymo Brunello, Societatis nostræ presbytero. Auctor orationis hujus est Sophronius patriarcha Hierosolymitanus, cujus anniversariam memoriam Græci et Latini agunt 2 die Martii. Græci hoc Elogio : « Sancti Patris nostri Sophr. patriarchæ Hierosolymitani, ex civitate Damasco, multiplici eruditione, divinarum litterarum scientia et pietate insignis. Floruit temporibus Heraclii, cujus anno 19 ad sedem illam evectus est, mortuus anno 28 ejusdem : « Cum, ut inquit Cedrenus, diu multumque adversus Heraclium, et cum eo sentientes Sergium, ac Pyrrhum Monothelitas, decertasset, » et multa scripta Ecclesiæ reliquisset ; inter quæ liber qui Pratum spirituale inscribitur ; Vita Mariæ Ægyptiacæ, varia Encomia in sanctos, duæ homiliæ in crucem ; et Epistola synodica ad Joannem Pontif. Max. et Sergium episcopum Constantinopolitanum. Vide Cedrenum et Zonaram in Heraclio. Habuit Sophronius orationem hanc pridie Exaltationis sanctæ crucis, nempe 13 Septembris ; quo die celebratur Hierosolymis dedicatio templi, quod Anastasis seu Resurrectio vocabatur. Typicum Sabæ, 13 die, Τὰ ἐγκαίνια τῆς ἁγίας Χριστοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἀναστάσεως · Dedicatio sanctæ Christi Dei nostri Resurrectionis. Et de hac resurrectione loquitur in tota hac oratione Sophronius ; non autem de festo Resurrectionis seu Paschæ.

en: Gretser wrongly gives 'Οἱ τῶν ἰατρῶν πάντες, πολλάκις' ('Medici plerumque omnes', doctors for the most part all); for the true reading, which the matter itself cries out and the Vatican codices confirm, is 'Οἱ τῶν ἰατρῶν παῖδες, πολλάκις' ('Medici sæpenumero': doctors' [assistants/children] often). Angelo Mai, Spicilegium Romanum, vol. IV, preface, p. ix.
